project: kcl/thttpserver — a minimal HTTP server on kklass with GNU netcat as the network backend; kcl addition with own names (THttpRequest, THttpResponse, THttpRouter, THttpRouteObject, THttpServer, THttpApplication) plus a transport seam (THttpTransport, TNetcatTransport with two pre-spawned listener slots, TReplayTransport). FPC fcl-web is a design reference only. Goal: demonstrate kklass, not a full web server.
status: IN PROGRESS — P0 done 2026-09-29 (messages + replay transport, 137 unit tests); P1–P3 pending. PLAN.md written 2026-09-27, D6–D9 added and a critic pass folded in 2026-09-28 (3 blockers, 11 majors, 12 minors, nits; PLAN §8).

decisions.D1: own kcl names: kcl/thttpserver, THttp* classes; FPC fcl-web is a design reference only (recommendation was FPC-anchored kcl/fphttpserver — overruled)
decisions.D2: GNU netcat only + TReplayTransport test double
decisions.D4: AcceptIdleTimeout default 0 (off, as FPC); tests always set 1000 ms
decisions.D5: pre-spawn the next listener right after the current request line arrives, in P2; two FIFO-backed slots (bash allows one coproc); fallback to a single coproc listener if the FIFO mechanics prove unreliable on msys — owner to be told — critic 2026-09-28: feasible only with an O_WRONLY writer, the child closing the other slot's fds, a cat stdin relay and a drained close (PLAN §2.5); re-verified by the supervisor 3/3 on both bashes
decisions.D6: request fields are read-only properties over private fields (property X read _x); generalised by critic C7 to every field another object reads. Measured: a plain var of another object read directly prints and leaves RESULT unchanged (stale); a property read is silent + RESULT; a write to a read-only property is rc 1 with kklass's own stderr line
decisions.D7: RegisterRoute PATTERN METHOD HANDLER [ISDEFAULT [DATA]] (with >=3 args the 2nd is always METHOD); route object gets DATA in RouteData, function / inst.method handler as $3; stored in ${inst}_rdat (never _data)
decisions.D8: an abstract route class is refused at registration with rc 2, by reading ${CLASS}_class_abstract (the flag .new checks) — no probe instance (critic C17); roadmap note: a public kk.isAbstract in kklass
decisions.D9: THttpApplication.ServerClass (default THttpServer) so a descendant server plugs in; non-server class -> Initialize rc 2

planning_measurements.coproc_cycle: coproc nc -l -c -s 127.0.0.1 -p PORT; handler in the parent shell, state persists across requests (3/3), both bashes
planning_measurements.one_nc_many_clients: impossible with GNU 0.7.1: no -k; client 2 refused while the process lives on
planning_measurements.port_released_on_accept: nc #2 binds the same port while nc #1's accepted connection is still open, and receives client 2
planning_measurements.busy_port: rc 1 after ~74 ms, stderr 'Error: Couldn't setup listening socket (err=-3)'
planning_measurements.throughput: ~100 ms per request end-to-end (20 sequential curl requests, 5.3.9)
planning_measurements.object_cost: ~2.7 ms per request for object + TDictionary lifecycle, both bashes
planning_measurements.bytes: under C.UTF-8 ${#s} and read -N count characters; local LC_ALL=C counts bytes
planning_measurements.proxy: HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY=127.0.0.1:2080 on this machine — curl --noproxy '*' required
planning_measurements.fifo_rdwr_writer: 5.3.9: O_RDWR writer → nc never sees EOF after close, -c never fires (forbidden)
planning_measurements.fifo_wronly_writer: O_WRONLY → nc exits ~100 ms after close, client EOF ~32 ms, no open deadlock
planning_measurements.fifo_on_5_2: a Git-runtime FIFO as msys64 nc's stdin → 'select(core_readwrite): Bad file descriptor' on accept; < <(exec cat FIFO) relay fixes it
planning_measurements.fd_inheritance: pre-spawned listener inherits the live writer unless its child closes the other slot's fds
planning_measurements.working_variant: O_WRONLY + child closes other slot + cat relay + drained close: 3/3 on each bash (supervisor re-run 2026-09-28), 6/6 runs in critic probes incl. overlap; spawn 34-46 ms with relay, close 14-57 ms
planning_measurements.nc_w: -w limits accept only (not an accepted connection)
planning_measurements.nc_vv: 'Listening on IP PORT', 'Connection from IP:PORT', 'Listen mode failed: Connection timed out', 'Couldn't setup listening socket (err=-3)', 'Total received bytes: N'
planning_measurements.empty_assoc_key: a[$k]=1 with k='' aborts the whole top-level command (supervisor re-verified)
planning_measurements.printf_T_tz: local TZ ignored by %(...)T; TZ=UTC0 printf prefix works; names localized unless LC_ALL=C
planning_measurements.read_quirks: read -N does not count a dropped NUL; read -t 0 = rc 1 at once; -t -1 = error
planning_measurements.inherited_in_methods: bare inherited in a method passes no args; inherited in a destructor without a parent destructor = rc 127
planning_measurements.curl_expect: curl sends Expect: 100-continue only for bodies > 1 MiB

fact 2: byte lengths under local LC_ALL=C from LOCAL copies (5.2.37 nameref quirk, measured_p0.nameref_length); fact 3: SIGPIPE child with trap '' PIPE -> rc 1, silent, alive; without the trap rc 141 (pinned as the reason BeginServe ignores PIPE); fact 12: 53 raw request files through TReplayTransport + 413-not-read, 408-without-read and four open-pipe cases (408 x4, NUL 400 at once); fact 13: empty and hostile query keys, hostile header names/values, route params, marker assignment proves no abort, pwn never created; fact 14/15/19: 002 + 001 §5; fact 23: BASHPID, PATH='', stored-body grep over the four classes, plus a DEBUG-trap canary (set -T) with a positive control
per-request cost measured: ReadFrom of a 4-header GET from a file 3.1-3.3 ms; a 64 KiB body from a file ~80 ms, over a PIPE ~1.19 s (both bashes) — see measured_p0.pipe_body
deviations: Attach FD [ISHEAD [BANNER]]: a third optional argument + private var _banner (default 'kcl-thttpserver', '' = no Server line). §1.3 lists `Attach FD ISHEAD` only, but §2.3 requires the server's ServerBanner to be validated at send, so the response must receive it

validation failure -> 500 with the DEFAULT head: default banner and Content-Type, no custom header, empty body (Content-Length: 0); Code/CodeText/ContentType are updated to what was sent (so a later access log is truthful)
ContentSent becomes 1 on ANY write attempt, a failed one included (the server must never try a second write); SendContent before Attach is rc 1 (not 2)

SendRedirect only SETS (Code, CodeText '', Location) — FPC TResponse.SendRedirect semantics (httpdefs.pp:3047); CODE default 302, must be 300-399; URL non-empty without CR/LF; else rc 2 with nothing changed
Write joins its arguments with one space and appends verbatim, no newline
Content-Length must be plain digits within int64 (kk.isInt alone would accept '+3' and '007'); a repeated IDENTICAL Content-Length is kept once (not joined), a different one is 400

parser check order: request-line length 414 -> structure (exactly two SP, three non-empty parts) or any control character 400 -> version not HTTP/D.D 400 -> method 501 -> target not '/…' 400 -> version not 1.0/1.1 505 -> headers (431/400) -> HTTP/1.1 without Host 400 -> Transfer-Encoding 501 -> Content-Length 400/413 -> body; an empty request line is 400 (no RFC leading-CRLF skip)
header value: any control character other than HTAB is 400 (§2.2 names obs-fold only; RFC 9110 field-value), OWS trimmed on both sides
an error status leaves Method..Content empty; RemoteAddress and the headers read so far are kept
a code with no reason in the table is sent as `HTTP/1.1 299 ` (empty reason, SP kept); Content-Type is omitted when ContentType is '' and for 1xx/204; Server is omitted when the banner is ''

query: names are percent-decoded too; a NAME with %00 is skipped; a VALUE with %00 marks the name rejected (QueryField rc 1) and, being the first occurrence, a later valid one does not replace it; `?g` gives g = '' rc 0

TReplayTransport: capture path `<request file>.N.out` (N = accept ordinal, ResponseFile N); per-instance arrays `_rqf`/`_rsf`, private `_next`; Accept's RESULT = the ordinal; an Accept with a connection still open closes it first; Shutdown only closes the current connection; IDLE_MS/REQ_TIMEOUT_S ignored; AddRequestFile rc 1 for a non-regular / unreadable file; ResponseFile rc 1 for a non-integer index too
HasHeader '' is rc 2 (+ one kk.debug line), consistent with GetHeader ''
HeaderNames also refuses the `__THS_` prefix (an OUTARR named __THS_REASON would clobber the reason table)
SendContent does not (cannot, fork-free on 5.2) ignore SIGPIPE itself: the caller must — THttpServer.BeginServe does (§2.6)
fork-free proof: a 4th part (DEBUG-trap canary under set -T, positive control included) beyond PLAN §4's three; the body grep ignores `$((` (arithmetic) and `||` (not a pipe)

measured_p0.nameref_length: bash 5.2.37: `${#v}` of a kklass var (declare -n v="inst_data[v]") is 0; 5.3.9 gives the real length. Repro: class with `var _m`, body `_m=GET; kk._return "${#_m}"` -> 0 on 5.2.37, 3 on 5.3.9; `${_m:1}` and `${_m%T}` work on both. Take lengths from a local copy
measured_p0.epochrealtime_locale: EPOCHREALTIME uses the locale's decimal separator: `1790634659,903380` under LC_ALL=ru_RU.UTF-8 — the unit uses `${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/}`
measured_p0.nul_in_line: `IFS= read -r -n 8194` over `ab\0cd\n` gives `abcd` rc 0, silently (both bashes): a NUL in the request line or a header is dropped, not detectable; only a body NUL is 400
measured_p0.pipe_body: `read -d '' -n N` reads a PIPE one byte per syscall: a 65536-byte body takes ~1.19 s over a pipe vs ~80 ms from a file (both bashes) — relevant to P2's per-request model (§2.8) with MaxContentLength 65536
measured_p0.exec_group_idiom: `{ exec {fd}<missing; } 2>/dev/null` fails with rc 1, prints nothing and leaves the shell's stderr intact; no fd leak on success (fd count +2 per Accept, back to the start after CloseConnection)
measured_p0.sigpipe_exit: a write to a pipe whose reader is gone kills a bash without `trap '' PIPE` with rc 141 (preserved through `timeout`)
measured_p0.sweep_duration: one `bash tests/tests.sh` on 5.2.37 exceeded 590 s on 2026-09-29 (suite 14/29 reached); split runs total ~970 s (5.2.37) / ~915 s (5.3.9)

found_in_P0: the 5.2.37 `${#nameref-to-assoc-element}` = 0 quirk (measured_p0.nameref_length) can hit any kklass member body that takes `${#var}` of a stored var directly; a grep over the other kcl units found no such use; worth one line in kklass_book (not changed here)
